subject: Region redirect: traffic migration & validation
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Baker <tom.baker@finpay.com>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@finpay.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 07:12:00 +0000
Subject: Region redirect: traffic migration & validation

Tom / Liam —

Quick heads-up from the ops team: late last night (2026-12-07 22:50 UTC) we observed a sustained peering interruption affecting a subset of eu-west cloud links that serve third-party caching and egress for EU tenants. That manifested as elevated 5xx rates for a small percentage of EU-region requests and intermittent increased latency. Automated routing reduced the surface area, but we want to give impacted customers the option to switch their live traffic to an alternate region while we complete the peering restore and verification.

What happened (short):
- Peering degradation between eu-west and our CDN provider caused KV-cache misses and occasional connection timeouts for some endpoints.
- Our smart-routing layer detected the anomaly and started redirecting new requests to fallbacks; this kept most traffic healthy but increased token latency for affected sessions.

Two options for you:
1) Allow Redwood to redirect your tenant to our us-east fallback pool (automatic, zero config from your side). This is quickest.
2) Opt for a controlled DNS/endpoint swap we coordinate with your infra team (preferred if you want to preserve EU egress logs locally).

We attached a lightweight checklist with the exact steps (redwood-reroute-checklist.pdf). Key notes:
- If you choose option 1, expect a short period of KV-warmup (typical 30–90s) and a transient 100–200ms median token latency increase while caches fill.
- Option 2 requires a TTL flip you can do (we recommend 60s) and a pre-signed endpoint we will provide.

Request — can you confirm which option you prefer and an approximate cutover window? If you approve option 1 we can enact the redirect within 10 minutes of your confirmation and will monitor token-level SLOs.

We will follow with a tech-runbook that includes curl commands and a verification checklist. If you have data residency constraints we will also document what traffic and logs will move during the temporary redirect.

Apologies for the disruption — we are prioritizing verification and will share a post-incident timeline and RCA once validation completes.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0198

Attachment: redwood-reroute-checklist.pdf

> Tom / Liam —
> 
> Quick heads-up from the ops team: late last night (2026-12-07 22:50 UTC) we observed a sustained peering interruption affecting a subset of eu-west cloud links that serve third-party caching and egress for EU tenants...

Thanks for the quick note. We started seeing elevated errors on Tuesday morning (around 07:00 UTC) — identical symptoms. Two quick questions before we decide:
1) If we allow Redwood to switch to us-east, will any customer PII or EU audit logs be transferred out of EU during the redirect? We have compliance constraints.
2) Can you give an exact endpoint host we would point to if we do the controlled swap? We'll need that to run a staged test.

Short answer: we prefer the controlled DNS swap (option 2) to preserve residency, but we need a 30-minute maintenance window. Are you able to schedule that in the next 2 hours? If not, we may accept an automatic redirect for short-term mitigation.

Tom Baker
Head of Platform Ops | FinPay
O: +44 20 7946 0210

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Baker <tom.baker@finpay.com>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@finpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 08:03:47 +0000
Subject: Re: Region redirect: traffic migration & validation

Tom —

Thanks for the rapid reply and the preference. Short answers up front:
- Data residency: For both options we do not move persistent customer data stores. Logs and transient inference request metadata are handled according to the tenant configuration. For option 1 (automatic us-east failover) ephemeral request metadata (timestamps, non-persistent logs) will traverse us-east while the redirect is active. We will provide a complete log export of the period on request.
- Controlled endpoint: below is the host you can point at for a staged flip. We will also provide a temporary TLS cert and signed key:
  * staging endpoint (us-east): prod-redirect-ue1.redwood.ai
  * TTL recommendation: 60s

Runbook (high-level):
1) Pre-checks (you): confirm that your egress policies allow connections to prod-redirect-ue1.redwood.ai and that your firewall allows outbound on TLS/443.
2) Redwood prep (us): we will spin up an isolated fallback pool for your tenant and pre-warm KV caches with your most recent prompt prefixes.
3) DNS flip (you): change A/CNAME to prod-redirect-ue1.redwood.ai, wait for <TTL> (60s), run verification tests below.
4) Verification (you + us): run end-to-end checks: sample generation, stream latency, and a small 10k-token quality spot-check.
5) Rollback (you): revert CNAME to original and notify us; we will drain requests and validate cache state.

Verification commands (examples):
- Health check: curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://prod-redirect-ue1.redwood.ai/v1/health
- Sample generate: curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"input":"Hello"}' https://prod-redirect-ue1.redwood.ai/v1/generate

Expected impact during swap: median token latency may temporarily increase by ~120–250ms during warmup, error rates should drop to baseline within 2 minutes after swap if all prechecks pass.

I attached a short connectivity log we captured during the spike (connectivity-log-20261207.zip). We'll also coordinate a 30-minute maintenance window starting at a time you choose. If you want, Ben can assist with the DNS propagation checks and Evelyn will run token-level monitoring during the cut.

If you'd like us to schedule the window now, propose a start time and we'll claim it in our ops calendar.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Principal Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

Attachment: connectivity-log-20261207.zip

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Baker <tom.baker@finpay.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Region redirect: traffic migration & validation

Tom —

Thanks for confirming the preference for a controlled swap. Proposed window: 2026-12-09 18:30–19:00 UTC (30 minutes). If that works for your team, we'll:
- Reserve the fallback pool and pre-warm caches (Naomi)
- Provide the temporary TLS cert and endpoint IPs 20 minutes prior to start (Ben)
- Run token-quality spot checks and monitor SLOs (Evelyn)

Checklist for the cut (copy of the attached):
- Confirm firewall egress to prod-redirect-ue1.redwood.ai:443
- Provision test API key for staging verification (we will provide)
- Set DNS TTL to 60s (we recommend you reduce it 30–60 min before)
- Coordinate Slack channel with our ops team (we'll create #inc-20261207-finpay)

Postmortem and follow-up: we will publish a preliminary timeline within 24 hours of the completed swap and a full RCA within 5 business days. We'll include compensating controls and a recommended long-term mitigation for persistent peering issues. If you would like a joint postmortem session, propose 60 minutes between 2026-12-13 and 2026-12-15 and we'll schedule.

Please confirm the 18:30 UTC window and I'll lock it in and share the temporary cert details.

Appreciate your flexibility — we'll keep this as tight as possible.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
